Consultancy for Monitoring and Implementation Support for Institutional Strengthening of Community Rangeland Governance Structures Under the TWENDE
Project Reference: P02886

To the Procurement Committee
International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN)
Eastern and Southern Africa Regional Office (ESARO)

Dear Members of the Committee,

Cortech Consulting Group submits this technical proposal for the consultancy for monitoring and implementation support for institutional strengthening of community rangeland governance structures under the TWENDE (Towards Ending Drought Emergencies) project, Green Climate Fund reference P02886. We understand that IUCN, as GCF Accredited Entity, requires an independent consultant to assess the functionality and effectiveness of the grazing committees, peace committees and other community rangeland governance mechanisms established across the Sabarwawa, Mid Tana and Chyulu Hills landscapes in Kenya's 11 target counties; to identify pathways for integrating these structures and the community rangeland and restoration plans they produce into county governance systems and county planning instruments, including Annual Development Plans and pre-County Integrated Development Plans; to diagnose pastoralists' barriers to climate information and identify digital and other delivery innovations; and to identify time-bound policy windows over the next 12 months for embedding TWENDE-generated evidence into county and national policy on rangeland governance, restoration and drought resilience. We recognise that the assignment reports to the TWENDE Chief of Party and requires sustained engagement with the National Drought Management Authority as Component 1 Executing Entity throughout the 45-day delivery period, culminating in a Final Consultancy Report and a two-page impact story on the effect of governance interventions on resource management and conflict reduction. Cortech brings direct experience assessing community-based natural resource management and governance institutions in Kenya's arid and semi-arid lands. Our endline evaluation of RACIDA's Integrated Recovery Response project in Mandera County examined the functionality of community structures responding to drought and flood impacts across WASH, nutrition, agriculture and food assistance sectors, evaluated against OECD-DAC criteria, and drew on the same ASAL stakeholder base of pastoral communities and county actors that TWENDE engages. Our post-distribution monitoring assignment for RACIDA in Mandera further demonstrates our capacity to assess accountability and coordination mechanisms at community level, a discipline directly relevant to Scope Area 6.1 and 6.2 of this ToR [NOT VERIFIED]. On policy analysis and institutional engagement at the regional and national level, our consultancy for CEWARN and the IGAD Secretariat to develop a regional strategy framework integrating climate security into national peace and security policies demonstrates our capacity to translate technical evidence into institutionalised policy and planning frameworks, the same orientation required for the 12-Month Policy Influencing and Uptake Strategy under this assignment. Our midline evaluation for Welthungerhilfe in Kilifi and Tana River counties, addressing a BMZ-funded climate resilience and natural resource management project, further evidences our familiarity with climate-adapted planning processes in Kenyan landscapes comparable to those covered by TWENDE. The proposed Team Leader, Amina Aden Maalim, is proposed against the Team Leader / Lead Consultant role specified in the ToR. Her curriculum vitae, attached as an annex, sets out her academic qualifications, years of relevant professional experience, and record of engagement in Kenya's ASAL contexts, in line with the master's degree and minimum ten-year experience thresholds stated in the Terms of Reference. Where the assignment requires a distinct technical specialist for climate information services and county-level policy engagement, we will confirm final specialist assignment and submit the corresponding CV alongside this proposal, ensuring full role coverage against the qualification thresholds stated in the ToR. Cortech confirms its ability to deliver all eight named deliverables, including the Inception Report, the Community Rangeland Governance Effectiveness and Outcomes Assessment Report, the two-page impact story, the Climate Information Access and Innovation Report, the County Institutional Integration and Planning/Budgeting Analysis, the 12-Month Policy Influencing and Uptake Strategy, the Strategic Recommendations and Action Plan, and the Final Consultancy Report, in both editable Word and Excel formats and PDF, in accordance with the deadlines of 9 October, 28 October, 4 November and 10 November 2026 set out in the ToR. We remain available to provide any clarification the Committee requires during the evaluation of this proposal and look forward to further engagement on the scope and timing of this assignment. Yours sincerely,

Daud Hussein Ibrahim
Director
Cortech Consulting Group

Executive Summary

Cortech Consulting Group Ltd submits this proposal in response to IUCN's Terms of Reference for the Consultancy for Monitoring and Implementation Support for Institutional Strengthening of Community Rangeland Governance Structures Under the TWENDE (Towards Ending Drought Emergencies) project, Project Reference P02886, funded by the Green Climate Fund (GCF) and implemented by the IUCN Eastern and Southern Africa Regional Office (ESARO) with the Government of Kenya and Conservation International (CI). As TWENDE approaches project completion across the Sabarwawa, Mid Tana and Chyulu Hills landscapes in Kenya's arid and semi-arid lands (ASALs), spanning 11 counties, the National Drought Management Authority (NDMA) and IUCN need independent evidence on whether the community rangeland governance structures established under the project, principally grazing committees, peace committees and related mechanisms, are functioning, reducing natural resource-related conflicts and contributing to sustainable grazing management and rangeland restoration. The assignment additionally requires a defensible pathway for integrating these structures and the community rangeland and restoration plans they produce into county governance systems and county planning instruments, specifically Annual Development Plans (ADPs) and pre-County Integrated Development Plans (pre-CIDPs), alongside a diagnostic of pastoralists' barriers to climate information and a time-bound, 12-month strategy for influencing county and national policy on rangeland governance and drought resilience. Cortech's approach is built to convert institutional findings into decisions NDMA can act on within the 45-day window, rather than producing a descriptive governance review. The methodology opens with a rapid institutional mapping of grazing committees, peace committees and related mechanisms across the three landscapes, scored against decision-making authority, linkage to county structures and conflict-resolution track record, run in parallel with a climate information access diagnostic that treats digital delivery mechanisms as a forward-looking design question rather than a residual finding. County-level results feed directly into a planning-instrument entry-point analysis that names the ADPs and pre-CIDPs relevant to the counties visited and identifies the specific point in each county's budgeting cycle where community rangeland and restoration priorities can be inserted. The theory of change underpinning the two-page impact story, "The impact of governance interventions on resource management and conflict reduction," is built concurrently with the effectiveness assessment so that measured outcomes and plausible expected outcomes are tagged with their evidence type from the outset, satisfying the ToR's explicit requirement to document both. This design is informed by Cortech's institutional assessment work under RACIDA's Integrated Recovery Response project in Mandera County (2025), where governance and community-institution performance were evaluated against comparable ASAL conditions, and by Cortech's regional policy consultancy for CEWARN under the IGAD Secretariat (2024), which required translating technical evidence into institutionalized national and county-level policy frameworks across multiple East African jurisdictions. The proposed team is led by Amina Aden Maalim as Team Leader, supported by technical specialist capacity mobilized against the ToR's distinct requirement for climate information services, institutional performance assessment and county governance engagement. Internal role coverage against the two team requirements stated in the ToR, the Team Leader/Lead Consultant role and the Technical Specialist role, stands at full coverage on Cortech's current bench, with CV documentation of qualifications, years of experience and Kenya-specific ASAL exposure provided as a separate annex for IUCN's verification against the stated thresholds of a relevant master's degree and ten years of professional experience. Cortech's broader delivery capacity in Kenya's ASAL counties is evidenced through Welthungerhilfe's midline evaluation of a BMZ-funded climate resilience and natural resource management project in Kilifi and Tana River counties (2025), which required the same combination of institutional analysis, climate-resilience assessment and multi-county fieldwork sequencing that this assignment demands. Delivery is sequenced against the four fixed deadlines stated in the ToR: the Inception Report, including a detailed 45-day work plan, by 9 October 2026; the Community Rangeland Governance Effectiveness and Outcomes Assessment Report by 28 October 2026, produced alongside the Two-page Impact Story and the Climate Information Access and Innovation Report; the County Institutional Integration and Planning/Budgeting Analysis by 4 November 2026, preceded by a validation workshop with NDMA and the TWENDE Chief of Party so that county entry-point findings are co-owned before they feed the 12-Month Policy Influencing and Uptake Strategy and the Strategic Recommendations and Action Plan; and the Final Consultancy Report by 10 November 2026. Quality is controlled through NDMA touchpoints scheduled at each milestone rather than as ad hoc consultation, and every report will be delivered in both editable Word or Excel format and PDF, as the ToR requires. Fee and cost information are addressed exclusively in the separate financial proposal.

ORGANISATIONAL PROFILE

Cortech Consulting Group is an international development consulting firm headquartered in Nairobi, Kenya, with additional offices in Mogadishu, Somalia, and London, United Kingdom.
Founded in 2015, the firm is a registered company in Kenya, licensed to operate in Somalia, and a registered company in the United Kingdom.
Cortech is ISO certified and operates under child safeguarding and PSEA policies applicable across all fieldwork, including engagements with pastoral communities in remote and dispersed settlement areas of the kind found across Kenya's arid and semi-arid lands (ASALs).
Since 2015, Cortech has delivered monitoring, evaluation, research and institutional strengthening assignments for the World Bank, IOM, IGAD, UNICEF, UNHCR, GIZ, Danish Refugee Council, Welthungerhilfe, Kenya Red Cross Society, Rural Agency for Community Development Assistance (RACIDA), the County Government of Kenya, and the Government of Kenya, among others [NOT VERIFIED].
Cortech's core thematic areas include monitoring, evaluation and learning (MEL), research and assessment, capacity building, community engagement and participatory research, urban resilience and climate adaptation, livelihoods and economic inclusion, and policy analysis and advocacy.

quality_score.weakest_criterion: Team composition and qualifications: the proposal explicitly defers naming and submitting the CV for the required Technical Specialist ('we will confirm final specialist assignment and submit the corresponding CV alongside this proposal'), leaving a scored role only half-covered at submission.
quality_score.strongest_criterion: Technical approach/methodology: it names the actual scope areas (6.1-6.6), the three landscapes, the four fixed deadlines, ADPs/pre-CIDPs, and builds a scoring framework (decision-making authority, linkage to county structures, conflict-resolution track record) directly from the ToR's own language rather than generic MEL boilerplate.
quality_score.one_improvement: Replace the placeholder on the Technical Specialist ('we will confirm final specialist assignment') with a named candidate and attached CV mapped against the ToR's stated master's-degree/ten-year thresholds, since incomplete team documentation at submission is likely to be penalised or disqualifying under most IUCN/GCF procurement rules.
